Container.Name: handoff
Container.Overview:
Handoff turns a file or folder on your server into a shareable download link with an expiry date.
Mount a folder the way you would for any container and browse it in the admin interface. Click a file to share it and it is served straight off the share, so nothing is copied and no extra disk is used. Or share a whole folder and Handoff zips it once with no compression, which is the fast option for photos and video since they do not compress anyway. You can also drag a file into the browser to upload it. Every link can carry an expiry, an optional password, and an optional download limit.
When a link expires it is deleted, along with anything Handoff created for it — an upload or a generated archive. Your mounted folder is read-only to Handoff — it is only ever read from, never written to or deleted from.
Note on disk space: generated archives are written to the Appdata path, so zipping a 40GB folder needs 40GB free there. On a default Unraid setup that is your cache SSD. Point Appdata at an array share if you plan to share large folders.
Downloads support HTTP range requests, so a 40GB file survives a dropped connection and resumes instead of restarting. Meant to sit behind your existing reverse proxy.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: share link file transfer download expiring url shortener send wetransfer
Container.Requires: A reverse proxy if you want links to work outside your LAN.

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: Port for the Handoff web interface.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Database, browser uploads, and generated zip archives live here. Needs room for the largest folder you plan to share — consider an array share rather than the cache SSD.

Config.Name: Library
Config.Description: The folder you want to browse and share files from, mounted read-only. Point it at a single share (for example /mnt/user/Photos) if you would rather not browse everything.

Config.Name: Admin password
Config.Description: Password for the upload interface. Minimum 8 characters — the container will not start without it. Download links are separate and do not need this.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: Optional. The outside address of this app, for example https://share.example.com. Set it so the links you copy are the ones your recipients can actually open.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the app runs as.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the app runs as.
